open_questions: Ground-based time-series photometry at one ephemeris to test for flat-bottomed 4523 ppm transit vs spot modulation and depth stability
Higher-resolution imaging/spectroscopy to rule out 1.8 arcsec blended EB given high RUWE and depth scatter
dossier.public_summary: The dip varies from undetectable to very deep between transits and between TESS sectors and even disappears, and one transit even looks negative. The 12.2-day period is twice the star's 6.19-day spot cycle on an active small star, with no clear image showing the dip is on the target. This pattern matches blended variability/false positives rather than a steady 3.3-Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Six transits are not consistent: one is undetected (negative depth) and one is 9000 ppm, 2x the others. Top three carry 0.884 of signal, so dip is built from few bad events, not a stable planet.
reasons.value: p_consistent 7.662093484672812e-14, share_of_top_3 0.884, outliers depth_ppm -257 sigma -5.2 and 9000 sigma 4.5

reasons.why: Depth changes by factor ~4 across sectors even within the same TESS-SPOC source, with p_constant far below 0.01. Real small planets do not vary by thousands of ppm this much; inconsistent depth matches the bad-transit pattern.

No on-target centroid. neighbour plausible_within_1px 1 at sep 1.8 arcsec needs 0.068 eclipse, could not establish dip is on target; combined with xgboost planet_rank 0.06 this supports false positive.
